taskDescription: Complete the crossword using key terms from PA H5 | Hemolytic Anemias.

words.clue: Premature destruction of red blood cells occurring before their normal 120-day lifespan.
Clinical condition resulting from RBC destruction exceeding bone marrow's compensatory capacity.
Process of red blood cell production that the bone marrow can increase up to eight-fold in response to haemolytic stimulus.
Type of haemolysis accounting for 80-85% of all red cell destruction, occurring primarily in splenic sinusoids and hepatic tissue.
Type of haemolysis where red cell membranes rupture directly within blood vessels, comprising 15-20% of cases.
Pigment derived from haemoglobin catabolism that causes jaundice when unconjugated levels are elevated.
Serum protein that binds free plasma haemoglobin and becomes markedly depleted in intravascular haemolysis.
Enlargement of the spleen caused by macrophage hyperplasia in haemolytic disease.
Clinical yellowing of skin and sclera resulting from elevated unconjugated bilirubin.
Urinary metabolite of bilirubin found in elevated amounts during extravascular haemolysis.
Presence of haemoglobin in urine, a characteristic laboratory finding of intravascular haemolysis.
